Oversight / Professional Agency: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
Training Topic / Competency Item: Employers shall instruct their window cleaning employees in the proper use of all equipment provided to them
Purpose: Ensures window cleaning employees are instructed in the proper use of the equipment provided to them
Approval Basis: Employer instructs its own window cleaning employees in the proper use of the equipment it provides under 8 CCR 3282(d); no external approval of the instruction.
Frequency: Before assignment to work from scaffolds or boatswain's chairs
Notes / Research Flags: CORRECTION 2 re-judge: previously rejected as unmapped_setting; window-cleaning is an occupational role reached in "all buildings" per the article's own scope clause, not an industry exclusion — anchors on role. | [AUTO] Impact basis: Subsection (d) requires employers to instruct window cleaning employees in the proper use of all equipment provided, and restricts assignment to work from scaffolds or boatswain's chairs to employees who have been properly trained. (confidence High) | [AUTO] Not enumerated: the General Industry Safety Orders container is cross_cutting, but this hazard has no plausible occurrence in a HealthStream care setting, so the obligation is emitted once, anchored on role rather than on a setting it does not reach. General instruction language with no enumerated content, so Other Training Reference. Role-anchored: window cleaning is a building-services function contracted or performed outside the care-delivery workforce, so no HSTM Setting is enumerated. [review finding F2] Requirement Level corrected from 'Other Training Reference' to 'Explicit Training'. classification-spec.md defines Other Training Reference as general language WITH NO STRUCTURE, emitted as Parent only with no Children; this obligation carries Children, and its Child restricts assignment to employees "properly trained to handle such equipment" - which is structure, so the Explicit Training trigger (an enumerated topic list) is met. Explicit Training (#10) is derived from this field and follows automatically. | Family: window cleaning and powered platform operator training (3282, 3286, 3294, 3298) - family anchor. Self-refutation check: the Division-approved anchorages and Title 24 references in 3282 are equipment and building approvals, not training approval. Cal/OSHA pattern: the employer designs, delivers and where required certifies the training; DOSH enforces by inspection and citation and does not pre-approve training content.
Interpretive Conditions: § 3286(a)(2) specifies the training that must precede use of boatswain's chairs and CDAs, so where the equipment the employer provides under § 3282(d) is a boatswain's chair or CDA the "proper use" instruction is the § 3286(a)(2) curriculum rather than an employer-defined one.
Regulatory Change Summary: Employers must instruct window cleaning employees in the proper use of all equipment provided to them, and only employees properly trained to handle such equipment may be assigned to work from scaffolds or boatswain's chairs.
Interpretive Summary: A hook tying assignment eligibility to prior instruction; supports an assignment-gating competence record rather than an enumerated curriculum.
Source Change Context: Employers shall instruct their window cleaning employees in the proper use of all equipment provided to them

Oversight / Professional Agency: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
Training Topic / Competency Item: Employees shall be trained in the use of boatswain's chairs and/or CDAs before they shall be permitted to use such equipment
Purpose: Ensures employees are trained in the use of boatswain's chairs and controlled descent apparatus before being permitted to use them
Approval Basis: Employer trains employees in the use of boatswain's chairs and CDAs before permitting use, on the topics enumerated in 3286(a)(2)(A); no external approval.
Frequency: Before they shall be permitted to use such equipment
Notes / Research Flags: CORRECTION 2 re-judge: previously rejected as unmapped_setting; boatswain's chair/CDA use is an equipment-triggered duty reached in any building per Article 5's scope, not an industry exclusion — anchors on role. | [AUTO] Impact basis: Subsection (a)(2)(A) requires employees to be trained in the enumerated boatswain's chair/CDA topics before being permitted to use the equipment; no record or evaluation duty is stated in this subsection. (confidence High) | [AUTO] Not enumerated: the General Industry Safety Orders container is cross_cutting, but this hazard has no plausible occurrence in a HealthStream care setting, so the obligation is emitted once, anchored on role rather than on a setting it does not reach. | Family: window cleaning and powered platform operator training. Self-refutation check: 'accepted by the Division' in 3286(a)(1)(B) governs suspension heights and 'approved independent anchorages' govern rigging hardware - equipment and operating approvals, not approval of the training. Cal/OSHA pattern: the employer designs, delivers and where required certifies the training; DOSH enforces by inspection and citation and does not pre-approve training content.
Related Regulatory Provisions: 8 CCR Article 6, Appendix C, Section I (General Industry Safety Orders)
Interpretive Conditions: § 3282(p)(1)(C) requires an Operating Procedures Outline Sheet for each installation, which is the rigging and support-line configuration the (a)(2)(B) "proper rigging of support lines" topic must be taught against; Article 6, Appendix C, Section I supplies the personal fall arrest system requirements that fix the content of the "fall arrest systems" topic.
Regulatory Change Summary: Employees must be trained in rigging, line and anchorage inspection, safe use, fall arrest systems and self rescue before being permitted to use boatswain's chairs or controlled descent apparatus.
Interpretive Summary: Supports a before-first-use suspended-access training assignment with five enumerated subjects.
Source Change Context: Employees shall be trained in the use of boatswain's chairs and/or CDAs before they shall be permitted to use such equipment
